name: Lost
blurb: Plane-crash survivors on a mysterious island face its secrets, its people and each other
title: Lost Recap: Every Season and the Ending Explained
description: Lost recap: the main characters, what happens in all six seasons of the island mystery, and the 2010 finale explained, including the flash-sideways church.
h1: Lost Recap: Every Season and the Ending Explained
answer: Lost is an American drama series created by Jeffrey Lieber, J. J. Abrams and Damon Lindelof, with Lindelof and Carlton Cuse as showrunners. It aired on ABC from September 2004 to May 2010, six seasons and 121 episodes. Oceanic Flight 815, flying from Sydney to Los Angeles, breaks apart over a remote Pacific island, and the survivors must stay alive while waiting for a rescue that never comes. Each episode also tells one survivor's past in flashbacks, while the island reveals a smoke monster, hidden stations and other people already living there.

head: Character
Who they are
rows: Jack Shephard
A spinal surgeon who becomes the survivors' reluctant leader
Kate Austen
A fugitive who was being escorted by a U.S. marshal when the plane went down
James "Sawyer" Ford
A sarcastic con man who looks out for himself first
John Locke
A man of faith who believes the island brought him there for a reason
Hugo "Hurley" Reyes
A good-natured lottery winner who thinks his numbers are cursed
Sayid Jarrah
A former Iraqi Republican Guard communications officer with a violent past
Charlie Pace
A rock bassist trying to give up heroin
Sun and Jin Kwon
A Korean couple whose marriage is strained by her father's criminal business
Desmond Hume
A Scotsman the survivors find living underground on the island
Ben Linus
A soft-spoken, manipulative man the survivors capture in season 2

ol: Season 1 (2004–05): The 48 or so survivors set up camp on the beach. Jack takes charge, Locke, who was paralyzed before the crash, can suddenly walk, and the group meets a smoke monster in the jungle and a French woman, Danielle Rousseau, stranded for 16 years. Mysterious islanders the survivors call the Others kidnap the pregnant Claire. Boone dies after a fall. Michael builds a raft and leaves with his son Walt, Sawyer and Jin, but the Others take Walt. Jack and Locke blow open a metal hatch in the ground.

Season 2 (2005–06): The hatch is the Swan, a station built by the DHARMA Initiative, a 1970s research project. Desmond has spent three years inside entering a code every 108 minutes, told it stops a catastrophe. Survivors from the plane's tail section join the camp. The group captures a man calling himself Henry Gale, who is really Ben Linus, the Others' leader. Michael kills two survivors to free Ben in exchange for Walt and leaves the island. Locke stops entering the code, and Desmond turns a failsafe key that destroys the hatch.

Season 3 (2006–07): The Others hold Jack, Kate and Sawyer on a smaller island. Ben has a tumor, and Jack operates on him in return for a promised way home. Desmond begins seeing flashes of the future, including Charlie's death. Locke meets the Others and hears of their unseen leader, Jacob. Charlie drowns in an underwater station after learning that the ship offshore is not the rescue it seems. The finale's flashback is a flash-forward: Jack, off the island, insists they have to go back.

Season 4 (2008): A freighter sent by businessman Charles Widmore arrives, carrying a team of mercenaries. Ben moves the whole island by turning a frozen wheel and is thrown off it. Six survivors, called the Oceanic Six, are rescued and lie about what happened. Back home, Jack learns that the man in the coffin is Locke.

Season 5 (2009): Those left behind jump uncontrollably through time until Locke leaves to stop it. The Oceanic Six return on Ajira Flight 316; some land in 1977, where Sawyer, Juliet and others have spent three years living with DHARMA. Physicist Daniel Faraday plans to set off a hydrogen bomb to stop the accident that caused the crash, and Juliet detonates it. In the present, the Locke who came back is not Locke but an enemy of Jacob, who tricks Ben into killing Jacob.

Season 6 (2010): The story splits. On the island, the Man in Black, the smoke monster wearing Locke's face, tries to leave and to kill the candidates chosen to replace Jacob; Sayid, Sun and Jin die. A second timeline, the flash-sideways, shows Flight 815 landing safely in Los Angeles. The season reveals that Jacob and the Man in Black are twin brothers, and that Jacob's role was to guard a source of light at the island's heart. Jack agrees to take Jacob's place.

body: In the finale, The End (May 23, 2010), Desmond removes a stone from the heart of the island, the light goes out and the Man in Black becomes mortal. Jack kills him, then climbs down to put the stone back and save the island. Kate, Sawyer, Claire and a few others escape on the Ajira plane. Hurley becomes the island's new protector, with Ben as his helper. The badly wounded Jack lies down in the bamboo field where he woke up after the crash and dies as the plane flies overhead.

In the flash-sideways, the survivors remember their lives on the island one by one and gather at a church. Jack's father, Christian Shephard, explains that they are all dead: they died at different times, some long after Jack, and made this place together so they could find each other before moving on. Light fills the church.

ul: Common misreading: the survivors were dead all along and the island was purgatory. The finale does not say that. Christian tells Jack that everything that happened to him was real, and Lindelof and Cuse repeatedly denied the purgatory theory while the show aired.
What the sideways world is: a shared afterlife or waiting room, not an alternate result of the bomb.
Why many viewers were frustrated: the finale focuses on the characters' arcs and leaves many island mysteries unexplained, and its quality is still debated.
Faith against reason: Locke's belief that the island has a purpose keeps clashing with Jack's insistence on facts, and Jack ends the story taking Locke's view.
Redemption: the flashbacks show every survivor running from something, and the island gives each a chance to become someone better.
Fate and free will: the candidates, the numbers and the time travel raise the question of whether anyone chose to be there.
Community: Jack's early warning that the survivors must stick together or die alone runs through the show, which keeps showing that they last only as a group.
Fathers and children: Jack, Locke, Kate, Sawyer and Ben are all shaped by broken relationships with their parents.
Length: six seasons, 121 episodes of about 42 minutes, plus a few double-length finales.
Original language: English, with Korean scenes for Sun and Jin. The show was filmed in Hawaii.
Structure: flashbacks in seasons 1–3, flash-forwards in season 4, time travel in season 5 and the flash-sideways in season 6; watch in order.
Content: violence and gunfights, character deaths, drug addiction and some disturbing scenes; no graphic sex.

check.q: What is in the hatch the survivors open?
options: A DHARMA Initiative station where a code must be entered every 108 minutes
The wreck of a second plane
check.why: The hatch is the Swan station, where Desmond has been entering a code every 108 minutes.

check.q: Who becomes the island's protector at the very end?
check.why: The dying Jack passes the role to Hurley, who asks Ben to help him.

check.q: What does the flash-sideways turn out to be?
options: A timeline created by the hydrogen bomb
A place the survivors made after death to find each other
check.why: Christian Shephard explains in the church that they are all dead and made this place to find each other and move on.

faq.q: Were they dead the whole time in Lost?
faq.a: No. The events on the island were real and the survivors lived through them. Only the season 6 flash-sideways takes place after death, and the characters arrive there at different times.

faq.q: What is the smoke monster in Lost?
faq.a: It is the Man in Black, Jacob's twin brother, who became the smoke after being thrown into the light at the island's heart. He can take the form of dead people, including Locke.

faq.q: How many seasons and episodes does Lost have?
faq.a: Six seasons and 121 episodes, aired on ABC from September 22, 2004, to May 23, 2010.
